Quantum I Ching

Binary Trigrams, Qubit Superpositions, and Yin–Yang Isomorphism

Formalizes the analogy between the I Ching binary structure (trigrams and hexagrams) and the quantum state space of qubits. It includes: (a) a table mapping trigrams to computational basis states; (b) a concise mapping from quantum concepts to I Ching concepts; and (c) a structural account of the logical isomorphism between yin–yang and quantum superposition

Trigrams as 3‑bit Binary States

Lines are counted bottom → top; yang = 1 (solid), yin = 0 (broken).

Trigram Name (Pinyin) Lines (bottom→top) Binary Decimal Qubit Basis
☰ Qián (Heaven) 1 1 1 111 7 |111⟩
☱ Duì (Lake) 1 1 0 110 6 |110⟩
☲ Lí (Fire) 1 0 1 101 5 |101⟩
☳ Zhèn (Thunder) 1 0 0 100 4 |100⟩
☴ Xùn (Wind) 0 1 1 011 3 |011⟩
☵ Kǎn (Water) 0 1 0 010 2 |010⟩
☶ Gèn (Mountain) 0 0 1 001 1 |001⟩
☷ Kūn (Earth) 0 0 0 000 0 |000⟩

Conceptual Correspondence

Quantum Concept I Ching Parallel Explanation
Superposition All trigrams/hexagrams latent Before casting, the system is a field of potential patterns (2^3 / 2^6 configurations).
Entanglement Correlative resonance Lines and trigrams interdepend; change in one part conditions the whole (感應).
Measurement / Collapse Divination (casting) The act of casting selects a definite configuration consistent with the context and inquiry.
Hilbert Space Dao as undivided field The space of all amplitudes parallels the undifferentiated whole from which patterns arise.
Unitary Evolution 易 (Yi) transformation Moving lines and hexagram change correspond to coherent transformations within state space.

Logical Isomorphism (Yin–Yang ↔ Qubit)

Aspect Yin–Yang Logic Qubit Logic
Basis States yin (0), yang (1) |0⟩, |1⟩
Composition Mutual containment, continuous balance Superposition: |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩
Geometry Taiji rotation (phase of balance) Bloch sphere (relative phase/amplitude)
Dynamics Alternation/Transformation (易) Unitary evolution
Observation Manifestation as yin or yang Projective measurement (collapse to 0 or 1)

Notes:

Three‑Qubit Space: Any state can be written as |Ψ⟩ = Σi,j,k∈{0,1} cijk|ijk⟩. Mapping |ijk⟩ ↔ trigram binary (bottom→top).
Hexagrams as Basis: Two stacked trigrams form 6 bits (2^6 = 64). Each hexagram ↔ a computational basis vector in a 6‑qubit Hilbert space.
Yin–Yang Isomorphism: Balance can be parameterized by an angle θ so that yang ∝ cos θ, yin ∝ sin θ, analogous to amplitudes on the Bloch sphere.
